result.title: MEND: RL For Flow Models via Proximal Velocity Matching
result.summary: Reward post-training of flow models either reweights the model's own samples under a KL penalty or a frozen reference, often for thousands of updates, or backpropagates the reward and moves every sample without checking that the move is worth its size. We introduce MEND, a reinforcement learning method built on proximal velocity matching. MEND caps rewards within each prompt group, so samples that already score well receive no move. Below the cap, it proposes moves along the reward gradient and accepts one only when its capped reward gain exceeds a quadratic displacement price. The model then regresses onto the resulting velocity targets, with no KL term, frozen reference model, or advantage weights. In 100 updates, MEND outperforms Flow-GRPO (about 4k updates) on five of six evaluators at the same distance to base-model images. Under an equal-budget protocol, it surpasses ReFL and DiffusionNFT at every evaluated update across four training rewards, reaching PickScore 24.03 versus 23.92 and 23.43, respectively. A 300-update three-reward run also surpasses the five-reward DiffusionNFT model on all three rewards it trains on. MEND is general and easy to adopt: it applies to any flow backbone with a differentiable reward.

AI.brief_summary: MEND 提出一种面向流模型（flow model）的强化学习后训练方法：以 proximal velocity matching 为核心，对同一 prompt 组内的奖励设上限，仅在奖励增益超过二次位移代价时接受沿奖励梯度提出的更新，再回归到相应速度目标，无需 KL 项、冻结参考模型或优势权重，并在较少更新步数下取得优于 Flow-GRPO 等方法的奖励表现。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作本身是图像生成模型的奖励后训练，不直接研究 VLM 推理，但其「奖励增益是否值得位移代价」的接受判据、分组奖励上限和速度目标回归，可能与 LVR 中的动态计算、停止决策与贡献分配问题存在概念联系，可供核查如何以代价换取推理状态更新。
